title: Create First-72-Hour Support Coverage Plan
summary: Michelle recorded the First-72-Hour Support Coverage Plan for launch (Monday 31 August 2026 00:00 America/New_York through Thursday 3 September 2026 00:00). The plan assigns support owners, backup coverage, severity mapping (support P1–P4 to incident SEV-1–SEV-4), response expectations, and escalation paths. It integrates existing Row 153 support operations, Row 154 / operating-system incident management, and the Launch-Day Runbook. No product, marketing, legal, Stripe, DNS, or authentication files were changed. Founder acceptance is not recorded.

support_priorities.published_architect_expectation: Typically respond within 3 days, with a goal of 72 hours or less. Urgent security and privacy concerns are prioritized. Do not promise a resolution time.

levels.label: Urgent
examples: Multiple Architects with the same critical failure
levels.first_72h_expectation: Not an ordinary three-day queue item. Acknowledge as urgent. Michelle routes immediately. Imani contains if technical/security. Founder if SEV-1 / Attention YES.

levels.label: High
examples: Individual cannot access a purchased experience
levels.first_72h_expectation: First human response inside 24 hours. Nia owns CX; Michelle routes payment/access; Imani if system failure.

levels.label: Normal
levels.first_72h_expectation: Stay inside the published 72-hour goal. Do not pull Founder into the queue.

levels.label: Low
levels.first_72h_expectation: Same 72-hour goal. Capture Voice-of-Architect themes for later rows; do not invent a second tracker.

code_default_ticket_owner.note: Default ticket assignee is routing, not a change of primary CX ownership. Nia remains primary public support. Michelle remains backup/routing. Imani is not auto-assigned as ticket owner; Imani is an escalation target.

severity_mapping_to_incidents.rule: Support priority is the Architect-ticket clock. Incident SEV is the production/risk clock from the operating system. Classify both. Do not invent a third scale.

map.when: Launch unavailable; payment broadly failing; material security/privacy; widespread access failure; material data-loss risk; severe participant-impacting production failure.
Urgent ticket that is not a broad outage (for example a serious individual security concern already contained, or a payment issue affecting one Architect that is not a checkout outage).
Material degradation affecting important functionality or a meaningful participant cohort (several Architects blocked from registration, Journey, Lumina, or paid access).
Contained individual defect with a workaround and no material launch threat.
Routine questions, feedback, cosmetic/non-critical defects. Do not open an incident for ordinary queue work.

support_surge.trigger: Open support backlog ≥ 10, or approaching/overdue 72-hour expectation

routes.founder: If Attention YES or severe participant-impacting production failure
routes.required_response: Experience diagnosis. Use approved public language only.
